thread:
Tomáš Novák: collecting notes for the postmortem writeup ("Overload learnings" section) + specifically: how circuit breakers / load shedding would have changed the outcome. pls drop bullets we can paste in.

Tomáš Novák: context: during the spike, we saw gateway 5xx/timeouts, routing RPC pileups, runtime queues backing up, then tail latency collapse. we mitigated w/ manual rate shaping + partial region shift, but customer impact lasted ~34 mins.

Rafael Mendes: main learning: we failed *late* (runtime) instead of failing *early* (edge). by the time we started timing out, we were already in retry-storm territory and control-plane was degraded.

Rafael Mendes: what breakers would change: deterministic shed at gateway (429/503 w/ Retry-After) based on per-(model, region, tier) capacity + breaker state -> reduces downstream load and keeps routing/control plane responsive.

Christine Wong: +1. breaker framing for writeup:
- current: soft backpressure but unbounded queues -> p99 skyrockets, then timeouts -> clients retry -> worse
- with breakers: bounded queue + open breaker => immediate reject w/ explicit overload code + cooldown/hysteresis
- half-open probes allow controlled recovery (no thundering herd)

Mina Haddad: add that routing was doing a lot of work even after we were "already dead". every request still hitting placement + capacity checks + fallback evals.

Mina Haddad: with breaker state store + memoized decisions we can short-circuit routing on open state (cheap check) and either (a) shed at edge or (b) route to known-good fallback if policy allows.

Ravi Menon: also: our capacity signals were there but not wired into an admission policy. we had GPU util pegged + queue depth trending up, but gateway still accepted.

Ravi Menon: in new world: breaker inputs include: gpu_pool_saturation, runtime_queue_depth, routing_rpc_latency, error rates; open threshold triggers before p99 collapses. (important: include hysteresis so it doesn’t flap.)

Allison Grant: observability bullets for postmortem:
- we lacked a single "overload is happening" panel; we had to piece from 5 dashboards
- no consistent labeling for shed/timeout reasons, so we couldn’t quantify what % was overload vs internal failure
- new metrics should separate "overload-protected" from "unexpected 5xx" for error budget + paging

Aisha Bello: paging angle: we paged hard on 5xx but didn’t have a way to say "we’re shedding intentionally".

Aisha Bello: with standardized overload errors + SLO accounting changes, oncall can treat shed-rate threshold as an overload event (monitor, maybe capacity action) vs Sev2 for random 500s.

Nora Ahmed: customer comms angle: impact was confusing because customers saw mixed 500/502/503 + timeouts; they didn’t know if retry helped.

Nora Ahmed: with taxonomy + headers:
- 429 + `Retry-After` for "admission denied" style
- 503 + `Retry-After` for "temporarily unavailable" (breaker open)
- consistent Redwood error code so SDKs can implement safe backoff

incident-bot: :notebook_with_decorative_cover: Postmortem draft doc updated: "Overload learnings" section placeholder added. <https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/POST/PM-2024-07-Overload-Event>

Sean Gallagher: please explicitly call out *cascading failure prevention*. the big win isn’t just nicer errors; it’s keeping core subsystems alive (routing, auth, quotas, billing hooks) so recovery is faster + blast radius smaller.

Sean Gallagher: i’d like one paragraph: "how we would have failed" w/ breakers: early shed at edge, bounded runtime queues, preserve control plane health, avoid retry amplification.

Christine Wong: breaker-specific paragraph suggestion:
"If per-(model,region,tier) breaker had been active, it would have opened once queue depth + saturation crossed threshold, returning 503 w/ Retry-After within ~30–80ms at gateway rather than holding connections until timeout. Cooldown + half-open probing would have limited re-admission to N RPS until capacity stabilized, preventing oscillations."  [reactions: :thumbsup: x4]

Rafael Mendes: don’t forget streaming: a bunch of impact was mid-stream disconnects. w/ shed points at prefill boundary we’d reject before starting stream (customer sees immediate overload error) vs dropping sockets mid generation.

Rafael Mendes: for postmortem: "prefer to shed *before* work begins". once we start decode, disconnects waste GPU time + hurt UX.

Mina Haddad: also fairness: in the incident, a few high-volume tenants dominated queue. without admission control by tier/tenant, we starved low-volume apps.

Mina Haddad: breakers + edge fairness (tier-aware) => protect baseline for long-tail tenants + keep internal control traffic (health checks, config fetch) from being crowded out.

Allison Grant: tracing note: we couldn’t see where time was spent once things got bad (gateway -> routing -> runtime). we need end-to-end reason propagation (`overload_reason`) in logs/traces, sampled but consistent.

Aisha Bello: for the writeup: "manual mitigation was risky": to stabilize we used ad-hoc rate shaping + region shift, but lacked a safe knob (feature-flagged breaker config) and clear rollback. breakers give us standardized, auditable switches + safer default behavior.

Nora Ahmed: customer-facing phrasing we should include: "During overload we may return 429/503 with Retry-After. This protects overall availability. These responses are not billed." (we should confirm billing but this is what support told customers during event.)

Christine Wong: one more learning: signal lag. GPU util updates were ~30s delayed in a couple regions, so any closed-loop breaker needs multiple signals (queue depth, scheduler latency) not only util.

Ravi Menon: +1. queue depth + runtime scheduler backlog are the earliest indicators. util can be misleading w/ long prompts (prefill heavy). add in writeup: "choose leading indicators".

Tomáš Novák: this is great. i’ll stitch into the PM section with: (1) what happened (late failure + retry amplification), (2) how breakers change failure mode (early, explicit, bounded), (3) why it reduces blast radius + improves recovery + comms.

Tomáš Novák: if anyone has a 1-2 sentence "counterfactual timeline" (e.g., breaker opens at t+3m, shed-rate rises, p99 stays < X), drop it.

Aisha Bello: counterfactual: based on graphs, queue depth crossed 2k at ~t+6m; if we opened at 1k + 2m cooldown, we’d have shed ~18% for ~12 mins instead of timing out ~45% for ~34 mins. i’ll add chart link to doc. <https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/overload-queue-depth?from=1721557000&to=1721562000>

Tomáš Novák: perfect, ty. [reactions: :white_check_mark: x2]
